36# ============================================================================= 

37# tle.gpu path 

38# ============================================================================= 

39# group norm is a row-reduce plus a row-affine over the SAME contiguous data: 

40# 

41# stats (N * group, group_size * HxW) -> mean, rstd one row per group 

42# affine (N * C, HxW) -> y = x * scale + shift 

43# one row per (batch, channel) 

44# 

45# Both rows are contiguous in a contiguous NCHW input, so both fit the 

46# `[XBLOCK, YBLOCK]` cluster-DMA tile that sum.py's `_tle_sum_row_kernel` uses: 

47# GM -> LM -> registers, no per-element GM pointer arithmetic. The fused 

48# GM-pointer kernel below walks the same bytes with `tl.load(X + base + idx)`, 

49# which is why it measured 0.06x of aten. 

50# 

51# TWO passes over the data, not one, and the reason is a hardware gap rather than 

52# taste. The hand-written XDNN kernel does group norm in ONE kernel 

53# (api/src/kernel/kunlun3cpp/kunlun3cpp_aten/group_norm_fwd.xpu): it gives each 

54# cluster a slice of the N * group groups, splits one group's `n` elements across 

55# SEVERAL CORES, and reduces across those cores through shared memory and a 

56# cluster barrier -- `sum_sm[transposed_cid] = sum; mfence_sm(); sync_all(); 

57# groupsum_sm(...)`, lines 968-973 -- after which every core has the group's mean 

58# and can apply the affine in the same kernel. 

59# 

60# tle.gpu has the shared-memory scope and the SM fence but NOT that barrier: the 

61# XPU op set is copy / normcopy / raw / dma_wait, and there is no `core_id()` 

62# either, because `tritonxpu-tle-core-tiling` is what assigns tile ROWS to cores. 

63# So a single tle kernel has to keep a whole group in one program, and that 

64# program's tile is only `group_size` rows -- 2 on the benchmark shapes, leaving 

65# 62 of 64 cores idle. That is exactly the corner the fused GM-pointer kernel 

66# below is in, and why it measured 0.06x of aten. 

67# 

68# Splitting at the barrier instead lets each pass pick the tile it wants. 

69_TLE_CORE_NUM = 64 

70# Program count the give-back loop aims for (one program per cluster). 

71_TLE_CLUSTERS = 8 

72# Fused single-kernel path (layernorm pattern): one program owns whole 

73# group-rows, reduces each row core-locally and normalizes it in place -- one GM 

74# read, one GM write, no barrier, the way tle_layernorm does it. It needs the 

75# WHOLE group-row resident in LM, so it only applies when the padded row width 

76# fits the per-core stack. test_tle_layernorm caps that at epc = XBLOCK*W/64 <= 

77# 256 (~20 B/element against an 8 KB stack); with XBLOCK == 1 that is a hard 

78# width ceiling of 256 * 64 = 16384 columns. Wider groups -- (16, 8, 128, 128) 

79# has group_size*HxW = 32768 -- fall back to the split stats/affine path. 

80# The SM computed-index gather this kernel needs is CORRECT as of the 

81# tritonxpu-tle-core-tiling fixes (anchor scan skipping [M,1] row-vector 

82# candidates, the cyclic 1D make_range, the bf16 SM load) -- see 

83# sm_gather_task/HANDOFF.md for the chain. 

84# Per-core element ceiling for the fused kernel's resident tile. Measured: at 

85# 512 elements/core the (16,16,1024) / (32,32,32,32) configs stopped compiling 

86# ("over the local-memory budget after pressure relief and vrf_budget 

87# escalation"), so 256 is the empirical cap rather than a derived budget. 

88_TLE_FUSE_EPC = 256 

89# WIDE segment budget: tile + two accumulator copies share the registers. 

90_TLE_FUSE_EPC_WIDE = 64 

91# Row-width ceiling. The wide-row segment loop has no residency limit, so this 

92# only guards against absurd widths (a mis-shaped view) rather than tuning. 

93_TLE_FUSE_WMAX = 1 << 16 

94# Wide-row two-pass loop threshold and segment width (elements). Above the 

95# threshold the m==1 fused kernel streams [1, RB] segments instead of holding 

96# the row; RB/64 is the per-core register footprint, so RB = 4096 -> 64 lanes. 

97_TLE_FUSE_LOOP_WMIN = 8192 

98_TLE_FUSE_LOOP_RB = 2048 

99# Row-block pipelining (hold-the-row path only). A program takes RITER row 

100# blocks instead of one and double-buffers them, so block i+1's GM read is in 

101# flight while block i is normalized -- the same DMA/compute overlap the 

102# hand-written XDNN kernel gets from its triple-buffered affine pass, but across 

103# ROW BLOCKS rather than column segments, so the input is still read exactly 

104# once (a column-segment two-pass has to re-read it). 

105# The lever it buys is per-core RESIDENCY: RITER row blocks at XBLOCK rows each 

106# do the work one block of XBLOCK*RITER rows would, at 1/RITER of the register 

107# footprint, without changing the program count. _TLE_FUSE_EPC_PIPE is the 

108# per-core element count the split aims for. It is a FLOOR, not a target, and 

109# measured: 64 gives mean 0.68x of aten on the core benchmark set, 32 gives 

110# 0.54x -- below 64 elements/core the tiles stop paying for their own loop 

111# (the (16,16,128) fp16 config blew up 40x at 32), so the halving stops there. 

112_TLE_FUSE_EPC_PIPE = 64 

113_TLE_FUSE_RITER_MAX = 8

117 torch.float32: tl.float32,

119}

122def _npo2(x): 

123 return 1 << (x - 1).bit_length() if x > 1 else 1

126@triton.jit( 

127 do_not_specialize=["L", "eps"], 

128 do_not_specialize_on_alignment=[ 

129 "x_desc", 

130 "y_desc", 

131 "W", 

132 "B", 

133 "mean_desc", 

134 "rstd_desc", 

135 ], 

136) 

137def _tle_group_norm_fused_kernel( 

138 x_desc, 

139 y_desc, 

140 W, 

141 B, 

142 mean_desc, 

143 rstd_desc, 

144 L, 

145 HW: tl.constexpr, 

146 eps, 

147 C: tl.constexpr, 

148 group_size: tl.constexpr, 

149 num_groups: tl.constexpr, 

150 XBLOCK: tl.constexpr, 

151 WT: tl.constexpr, 

152 CBLK: tl.constexpr, 

153 RB: tl.constexpr, 

154 WIDE: tl.constexpr, 

155 RITER: tl.constexpr, 

156 IN_DTYPE: tl.constexpr, 

157 OUT_DTYPE: tl.constexpr, 

158 CDT: tl.constexpr, 

159 TAIL: tl.constexpr, 

160 HAS_W: tl.constexpr, 

161 HAS_B: tl.constexpr, 

162): 

163 """Whole group norm for one tile of group-rows, the tle_layernorm way. 

164 

165 A program owns XBLOCK contiguous groups. With XBLOCK >= 2 the rows 

166 core-tile whole and the reduce is core-local (no barrier); with XBLOCK == 1 

167 the [1, WT] tile is LargeN -- the row splits across ALL 64 cores and the 

168 reduce goes cross-core through the standard smem+barrier path, which is what 

169 lets the widest rows (group_size * HxW = 32768) fuse at all. mean/rstd are 

170 computed and the row is normalized, one kernel, one launch. 

171 

172 WIDE rows (WT >= the loop threshold) hold too many per-core columns to sit 

173 in registers at once ("kernel stack over budget / vrf escalation"), so they 

174 take a TWO-PASS SEGMENT LOOP inside the same kernel: reduce segment by 

175 segment, then normalize segment by segment, over one [XBLOCK, RB] tile. The 

176 input is read from GM twice, but the launch count stays ONE and XBLOCK stays 

177 free to grow -- which is what keeps the program count down (a per-row 

178 program grid on a wide shape queues 16 waves on 8 clusters). 

179 

180 The per-channel weight/bias is the one thing layernorm does not have: within 

181 a group-row, column j belongs to channel `group*group_size + j // HxW`, and 

182 the group differs per row. Weight/bias are staged into cluster SHARED memory 

183 (smem, not per-core lmem) and indexed by that computed channel map with 

184 `local_ptr`. The scope matters: an LM `local_ptr` DROPS its index and hands 

185 back the core's own contiguous slice (that is how the `a` tile is 

186 addressed), so an LM weight buffer would ignore `ch` and multiply by the 

187 wrong lane -- measured as y off by 4.8 while mean/rstd stayed exact. Only 

188 the SM `local_ptr` honours an arbitrary index. Either way it stays off the 

189 GM-gather path that hangs the cluster. 

190 """ 

191 pid = tl.program_id(0) 

192 row0 = pid * XBLOCK 

193 rid = tl.arange(0, XBLOCK) 

194 rows = tl.broadcast_to(rid[:, None], (XBLOCK, WT)) 

195 cols = tl.broadcast_to(tl.arange(0, WT)[None, :], (XBLOCK, WT)) 

196 

197 if WIDE: 

198 # ---- two-pass segment loop over one [XBLOCK, RB] tile ---- 

199 # The residency here is the SEGMENT, not the row: [XBLOCK, RB]/64 

200 # elements per core. That is what lets XBLOCK grow on wide rows even 

201 # though the row cannot be held -- and XBLOCK is what keeps the program 

202 # count (and with it the wave count on 8 clusters) down. The tile 

203 # [XBLOCK, RB] core-tiles as LargeN when XBLOCK < 64, so each row's 

204 # segment reduce is cross-core across RB's column cores. 

205 srows = tl.broadcast_to(tl.arange(0, XBLOCK)[:, None], (XBLOCK, RB)) 

206 scols = tl.broadcast_to(tl.arange(0, RB)[None, :], (XBLOCK, RB)) 

207 buf = tle.gpu.alloc( 

208 [XBLOCK, RB], dtype=IN_DTYPE, layout=None, scope=tle.gpu.lmem 

209 ) 

210 buf_ptr = tle.gpu.local_ptr(buf, (srows, scols)) 

211 

212 # Deferred merge: accumulate the segments ELEMENT-WISE and run the 

213 # cross-core reduce ONCE, after the loop, instead of once per segment. 

214 # A per-segment `tl.sum` has to merge across the row's column cores 

215 # every iteration (smem write + cluster barrier + read back), and that 

216 # cost is what made the wide rows 5-10x slower than the split path. 

217 # The 2-D accumulators cost registers instead -- [XBLOCK, RB] each, 

218 # which is what the WIDE segment budget is sized for. 

219 acc = tl.zeros([XBLOCK, RB], tl.float32) 

220 acc_sq = tl.zeros([XBLOCK, RB], tl.float32) 

221 for coff in tl.range(0, WT, RB): 

222 # Only a segment that runs past L can be short, and only then is the 

223 # buffer worth clearing -- every other iteration overwrites it whole. 

224 # Zero-fill rather than `tl.where` on the loaded value: sum.py:217 

225 # records that the mask "returns wrong numbers in bf16 and blows the 

226 # LM budget in f16 at every tile size", and it also costs a live 

227 # [XBLOCK, RB] f32 beside two f32 accumulators that are already what 

228 # caps this leg (_TLE_FUSE_EPC_WIDE = 64, a third of the row budget). 

229 if TAIL: 

230 if coff + RB > L: 

231 tl.store(buf_ptr, tl.zeros([XBLOCK, RB], IN_DTYPE)) 

232 tle.gpu.copy(x_desc, buf, [XBLOCK, RB], [row0, coff]) 

233 xv = tl.load(buf_ptr).to(tl.float32) 

234 acc += xv 

235 acc_sq += xv * xv 

236 mean = tl.sum(acc, 1) / L 

237 var = tl.maximum(tl.sum(acc_sq, 1) / L - mean * mean, 0.0) 

238 rstd = rsqrt(var + eps) 

239 

240 if HAS_W or HAS_B: 

241 grp = (row0 + rid) % num_groups 

242 if HAS_W: 

243 w_smem = tle.gpu.alloc( 

244 [CBLK], dtype=IN_DTYPE, layout=None, scope=tle.gpu.smem 

245 ) 

246 tle.gpu.copy(W, w_smem, [C], [0]) 

247 if HAS_B: 

248 b_smem = tle.gpu.alloc( 

249 [CBLK], dtype=IN_DTYPE, layout=None, scope=tle.gpu.smem 

250 ) 

251 tle.gpu.copy(B, b_smem, [C], [0]) 

252 for coff in tl.range(0, WT, RB): 

253 tle.gpu.copy(x_desc, buf, [XBLOCK, RB], [row0, coff]) 

254 xv = tl.load(buf_ptr).to(CDT) 

255 yv = (xv - mean[:, None].to(CDT)) * rstd[:, None].to(CDT) 

256 if HAS_W or HAS_B: 

257 ch = grp[:, None] * group_size + ((coff + scols) // HW) 

258 if TAIL: 

259 ch = tl.minimum(ch, CBLK - 1) 

260 if HAS_W: 

261 yv = yv * tl.load(tle.gpu.local_ptr(w_smem, (ch,))).to(CDT) 

262 if HAS_B: 

263 yv = yv + tl.load(tle.gpu.local_ptr(b_smem, (ch,))).to(CDT) 

264 tl.store(buf_ptr, yv.to(IN_DTYPE)) 

265 tle.gpu.copy(buf, y_desc, [XBLOCK, RB], [row0, coff]) 

266 # mean/rstd leave through CLUSTER-SHARED SM, not a per-core LM strip. The 

267 # LM route makes all 64 cores issue a sub-cache-line s_lm2gm into the same 

268 # GM line and they serialise on it: measured +9.6us for a [16] f32 row and 

269 # +22us for f16, against +0.1-0.8us once one core sends the whole row 

270 # (sm_gather_task/strip_store_cost.py). SM honours a local_ptr index, so 

271 # every core can drop its lane in, and copy_l2g out of an smem buffer 

272 # coalesces the writeback into >= 64-byte chunks. bf16 rides the same SM 

273 # path as fp16/fp32 now that the XPU LLVM backend selects a bf16 store 

274 # into SM (addrspace(2)); it used to fall back to the LM strip because 

275 # XPU3 could not select that store and an f16-container bitcast did not 

276 # survive -- InstCombine in the O3 pass before llc folded the bitcast 

277 # away (backend/compiler.py's optimize_module(OPTIMIZE_O3)). 

278 m_lmem = tle.gpu.alloc( 

279 [XBLOCK], 

280 dtype=OUT_DTYPE, 

281 layout=None, 

282 scope=tle.gpu.smem, 

283 ) 

284 r_lmem = tle.gpu.alloc( 

285 [XBLOCK], 

286 dtype=OUT_DTYPE, 

287 layout=None, 

288 scope=tle.gpu.smem, 

289 ) 

290 tl.store(tle.gpu.local_ptr(m_lmem, (rid,)), mean.to(OUT_DTYPE)) 

291 tl.store(tle.gpu.local_ptr(r_lmem, (rid,)), rstd.to(OUT_DTYPE)) 

292 tle.gpu.copy(m_lmem, mean_desc, [XBLOCK], [row0]) 

293 tle.gpu.copy(r_lmem, rstd_desc, [XBLOCK], [row0]) 

294 else: 

295 # Weight/bias staging is common to both legs below and must happen ONCE, 

296 # before any pipelined prefetch: the smem copy carries its own 

297 # mfence(7)+barrier pair (the scope ignores `sync=`), and that fence 

298 # drains any in-flight DMA -- staging after a prefetch would cancel the 

299 # overlap it was issued for. Both buffers are always allocated so the 

300 # block helper can take them unconditionally; only the present ones are 

301 # filled (the launcher hands a dummy tensor for the absent one). 

302 w_smem = tle.gpu.alloc([CBLK], dtype=IN_DTYPE, layout=None, scope=tle.gpu.smem) 

303 b_smem = tle.gpu.alloc([CBLK], dtype=IN_DTYPE, layout=None, scope=tle.gpu.smem) 

304 if HAS_W: 

305 tle.gpu.copy(W, w_smem, [C], [0]) 

306 if HAS_B: 

307 tle.gpu.copy(B, b_smem, [C], [0]) 

308 if RITER > 1: 

309 # ---- double-buffered row blocks ------------------------------- 

310 # One program takes RITER blocks of XBLOCK rows and runs them two 

311 # per beat against two alternating tiles, so block i+1's GM read is 

312 # in flight while block i is normalized and block i-1 is written 

313 # back. Three things here are forced rather than chosen: 

314 # * the 2x unroll is MANDATORY -- a memdesc handle cannot be 

315 # selected by a runtime `it % 2`, so the two buffers have to be 

316 # two allocs and the loop two half beats; 

317 # * `dma_wait()` is a global, non-counting fence, so it goes AFTER 

318 # the compute it is meant to overlap; fencing right after the 

319 # prefetch re-serializes the loop; 

320 # * only the row tiles are double-buffered. The [XBLOCK] mean/rstd 

321 # strips are per-beat (m0/m1) because their copy-out is in 

322 # flight across the beat boundary too. 

323 base = pid * (XBLOCK * RITER) 

324 PAIRS: tl.constexpr = RITER // 2 

325 LASTROW: tl.constexpr = (RITER - 1) * XBLOCK 

326 a0 = tle.gpu.alloc( 

327 [XBLOCK, WT], dtype=IN_DTYPE, layout=None, scope=tle.gpu.lmem 

328 ) 

329 a1 = tle.gpu.alloc( 

330 [XBLOCK, WT], dtype=IN_DTYPE, layout=None, scope=tle.gpu.lmem 

331 ) 

332 # Per-beat stats buffers in cluster-shared SM, for the coalescing 

333 # reason documented in the WIDE leg above. 

334 m0 = tle.gpu.alloc( 

335 [XBLOCK], 

336 dtype=OUT_DTYPE, 

337 layout=None, 

338 scope=tle.gpu.smem, 

339 ) 

340 r0 = tle.gpu.alloc( 

341 [XBLOCK], 

342 dtype=OUT_DTYPE, 

343 layout=None, 

344 scope=tle.gpu.smem, 

345 ) 

346 m1 = tle.gpu.alloc( 

347 [XBLOCK], 

348 dtype=OUT_DTYPE, 

349 layout=None, 

350 scope=tle.gpu.smem, 

351 ) 

352 r1 = tle.gpu.alloc( 

353 [XBLOCK], 

354 dtype=OUT_DTYPE, 

355 layout=None, 

356 scope=tle.gpu.smem, 

357 ) 

358 a0_ptr = tle.gpu.local_ptr(a0, (rows, cols)) 

359 a1_ptr = tle.gpu.local_ptr(a1, (rows, cols)) 

360 m0_ptr = tle.gpu.local_ptr(m0, (rid,)) 

361 r0_ptr = tle.gpu.local_ptr(r0, (rid,)) 

362 m1_ptr = tle.gpu.local_ptr(m1, (rid,)) 

363 r1_ptr = tle.gpu.local_ptr(r1, (rid,)) 

364 # The pad is re-zeroed before EVERY refill, not once: the tiles are 

365 # reused each beat and normalized in place, so the previous beat's y 

366 # is sitting in those columns. Each zero sits immediately before the 

367 # async copy that refills that buffer -- the DMA lowering fences 

368 # before its transfer, so the store is visible, and the preceding 

369 # `dma_wait` has already retired that buffer's write-back. 

370 if TAIL: 

371 tl.store(a0_ptr, tl.zeros([XBLOCK, WT], IN_DTYPE)) 

372 tle.gpu.copy(x_desc, a0, [XBLOCK, WT], [base, 0], sync=False) 

373 tle.gpu.dma_wait() 

374 for it in range(0, PAIRS): 

375 b0 = base + (2 * it) * XBLOCK 

376 b1 = b0 + XBLOCK 

377 # The last prefetch runs past the program's blocks; clamp it 

378 # onto the final block (one redundant read, no wrong result). 

379 b2 = base + tl.minimum((2 * it + 2) * XBLOCK, LASTROW) 

380 # ---- half beat A: prefetch b1 -> a1, compute a0 (block b0) -- 

381 if TAIL: 

382 tl.store(a1_ptr, tl.zeros([XBLOCK, WT], IN_DTYPE)) 

383 tle.gpu.copy(x_desc, a1, [XBLOCK, WT], [b1, 0], sync=False) 

384 ch0 = ((b0 + rid) % num_groups)[:, None] * group_size + cols // HW 

385 if TAIL: 

386 ch0 = tl.minimum(ch0, CBLK - 1) 

387 x0 = tl.load(a0_ptr) 

388 xf0 = x0.to(tl.float32) 

389 mean0 = tl.sum(xf0, 1) / L 

390 var0 = tl.maximum(tl.sum(xf0 * xf0, 1) / L - mean0 * mean0, 0.0) 

391 rstd0 = rsqrt(var0 + eps) 

392 y0 = (x0.to(CDT) - mean0[:, None].to(CDT)) * rstd0[:, None].to(CDT) 

393 if HAS_W: 

394 y0 = y0 * tl.load(tle.gpu.local_ptr(w_smem, (ch0,))).to(CDT) 

395 if HAS_B: 

396 y0 = y0 + tl.load(tle.gpu.local_ptr(b_smem, (ch0,))).to(CDT) 

397 tl.store(a0_ptr, y0.to(IN_DTYPE)) 

398 tl.store(m0_ptr, mean0.to(OUT_DTYPE)) 

399 tl.store(r0_ptr, rstd0.to(OUT_DTYPE)) 

400 tle.gpu.copy(a0, y_desc, [XBLOCK, WT], [b0, 0], sync=False) 

401 tle.gpu.copy(m0, mean_desc, [XBLOCK], [b0], sync=False) 

402 tle.gpu.copy(r0, rstd_desc, [XBLOCK], [b0], sync=False) 

403 tle.gpu.dma_wait() 

404 # ---- half beat B: prefetch b2 -> a0, compute a1 (block b1) -- 

405 if TAIL: 

406 tl.store(a0_ptr, tl.zeros([XBLOCK, WT], IN_DTYPE)) 

407 tle.gpu.copy(x_desc, a0, [XBLOCK, WT], [b2, 0], sync=False) 

408 ch1 = ((b1 + rid) % num_groups)[:, None] * group_size + cols // HW 

409 if TAIL: 

410 ch1 = tl.minimum(ch1, CBLK - 1) 

411 x1 = tl.load(a1_ptr) 

412 xf1 = x1.to(tl.float32) 

413 mean1 = tl.sum(xf1, 1) / L 

414 var1 = tl.maximum(tl.sum(xf1 * xf1, 1) / L - mean1 * mean1, 0.0) 

415 rstd1 = rsqrt(var1 + eps) 

416 y1 = (x1.to(CDT) - mean1[:, None].to(CDT)) * rstd1[:, None].to(CDT) 

417 if HAS_W: 

418 y1 = y1 * tl.load(tle.gpu.local_ptr(w_smem, (ch1,))).to(CDT) 

419 if HAS_B: 

420 y1 = y1 + tl.load(tle.gpu.local_ptr(b_smem, (ch1,))).to(CDT) 

421 tl.store(a1_ptr, y1.to(IN_DTYPE)) 

422 tl.store(m1_ptr, mean1.to(OUT_DTYPE)) 

423 tl.store(r1_ptr, rstd1.to(OUT_DTYPE)) 

424 tle.gpu.copy(a1, y_desc, [XBLOCK, WT], [b1, 0], sync=False) 

425 tle.gpu.copy(m1, mean_desc, [XBLOCK], [b1], sync=False) 

426 tle.gpu.copy(r1, rstd_desc, [XBLOCK], [b1], sync=False) 

427 tle.gpu.dma_wait() 

428 else: 

429 a_lmem = tle.gpu.alloc( 

430 [XBLOCK, WT], dtype=IN_DTYPE, layout=None, scope=tle.gpu.lmem 

431 ) 

432 # Cluster-shared SM, for the coalescing reason documented in the WIDE 

433 # leg above: a [XBLOCK] LM strip writeback costs ~10us (f32) / ~22us 

434 # (f16) in cross-cluster cache-line contention, an SM one ~0.1-0.8us. 

435 m_lmem = tle.gpu.alloc( 

436 [XBLOCK], 

437 dtype=OUT_DTYPE, 

438 layout=None, 

439 scope=tle.gpu.smem, 

440 ) 

441 r_lmem = tle.gpu.alloc( 

442 [XBLOCK], 

443 dtype=OUT_DTYPE, 

444 layout=None, 

445 scope=tle.gpu.smem, 

446 ) 

447 a_ptr = tle.gpu.local_ptr(a_lmem, (rows, cols)) 

448 if TAIL: 

449 tl.store(a_ptr, tl.zeros([XBLOCK, WT], IN_DTYPE)) 

450 tle.gpu.copy(x_desc, a_lmem, [XBLOCK, WT], [row0, 0]) 

451 ch = ((row0 + rid) % num_groups)[:, None] * group_size + cols // HW 

452 if TAIL: 

453 ch = tl.minimum(ch, CBLK - 1) 

454 x = tl.load(a_ptr) 

455 xf = x.to(tl.float32) 

456 mean = tl.sum(xf, 1) / L 

457 var = tl.maximum(tl.sum(xf * xf, 1) / L - mean * mean, 0.0) 

458 rstd = rsqrt(var + eps) 

459 y = (x.to(CDT) - mean[:, None].to(CDT)) * rstd[:, None].to(CDT) 

460 if HAS_W: 

461 y = y * tl.load(tle.gpu.local_ptr(w_smem, (ch,))).to(CDT) 

462 if HAS_B: 

463 y = y + tl.load(tle.gpu.local_ptr(b_smem, (ch,))).to(CDT) 

464 tl.store(a_ptr, y.to(IN_DTYPE)) 

465 tl.store(tle.gpu.local_ptr(m_lmem, (rid,)), mean.to(OUT_DTYPE)) 

466 tl.store(tle.gpu.local_ptr(r_lmem, (rid,)), rstd.to(OUT_DTYPE)) 

467 tle.gpu.copy(a_lmem, y_desc, [XBLOCK, WT], [row0, 0]) 

468 tle.gpu.copy(m_lmem, mean_desc, [XBLOCK], [row0]) 

469 tle.gpu.copy(r_lmem, rstd_desc, [XBLOCK], [row0]) 

470 

471 

472def _tle_group_norm_fused( 

473 input, 

474 y, 

475 weight, 

476 bias, 

477 mean, 

478 rstd, 

479 m_grp, 

480 L, 

481 HxW, 

482 C, 

483 group_size, 

484 group, 

485 eps, 

486 tl_dtype, 

487): 

488 """ONE tle kernel for the whole operator; False only when it cannot run. 

489 

490 Every shape the aten semantics can produce is covered here: 

491 * xblock >= 2 rows per program -- RowTiled, reduce core-local; 

492 * xblock == 1 -- LargeN m == 1: the [1, WT] tile splits the row across all 

493 64 cores and the reduce goes cross-core; 

494 * wide rows (WT >= the loop threshold) -- the same kernel streams [1, RB] 

495 segments in a two-pass loop (reduce, then normalize), so no register or 

496 LM residency limit applies to the row width. 

497 The only declines left are hard ones: a row wider than WMAX even for the 

498 segment loop, or a per-core slice that still will not fit. 

499 """ 

500 # Pad the row width up to the core count: the m == 1 LargeN tiling needs 

501 # WT % coreNum == 0, and npo2(L) < 64 (tiny single-group rows) would leave 

502 # the core-tiling pass unable to engage. The padding columns are handled 

503 # by the TAIL machinery (masked out of the reduce, clamped out of the 

504 # gather, never written back). 

505 WT = max(_npo2(L), _TLE_CORE_NUM) 

506 if WT > _TLE_FUSE_WMAX: 

507 return False 

508 # Segment width for rows too wide to hold. Deciding it FIRST also decides 

509 # what the xblock growth below budgets against: a WIDE row's resident tile 

510 # is [xblock, RB], not [xblock, WT]. RB is capped so the per-core segment 

511 # footprint (RB/coreNum elements) leaves room for the accumulators, and 

512 # stays >= coreNum so the [xblock, RB] tile core-tiles. 

513 rb = min(WT, _TLE_FUSE_LOOP_RB) 

514 wide = WT >= _TLE_FUSE_LOOP_WMIN 

515 resident = rb if wide else WT 

516 # xblock growth: keep the core's slice of the RESIDENT tile plus the two 

517 # [xblock] fp32 accumulators inside the LM element budget, and stop when 

518 # more rows per program would no longer cut the program count. 

519 # _TLE_FUSE_EPC is the MEASURED per-core element ceiling for this kernel 

520 # (256; larger values compiled "over the local-memory budget" on the 

521 # (16,16,1024)/(32,32,32,32) shapes, so this is empirical, not a model). 

522 # The resident width is what it applies to, which is the whole point of 

523 # deciding RB first: a wide row budgets [xblock, RB] instead of 

524 # [xblock, WT], so xblock can still grow there. 

525 # The WIDE branch keeps two [XBLOCK, RB] fp32 accumulators beside the 

526 # segment tile, so its per-core register budget is roughly a third of the 

527 # hold-the-row budget (see the deferred-merge comment in the kernel). 

528 epc = _TLE_FUSE_EPC_WIDE if wide else _TLE_FUSE_EPC 

529 xblock = 1 

530 while xblock * 2 <= m_grp and (xblock * 2) * resident // _TLE_CORE_NUM <= epc: 

531 xblock *= 2 

532 # Give the grid back toward one program per cluster when rows are plentiful. 

533 while ( 

534 xblock > 1 

535 and -(-m_grp // xblock) < _TLE_CLUSTERS 

536 and -(-m_grp // (xblock >> 1)) > -(-m_grp // xblock) 

537 ): 

538 xblock >>= 1 

539 # The core-tiling pass must ENGAGE for the SM weight/bias gather to be 

540 # correct (a no-op pass leaves the default layout, whose gather/store slot 

541 # counts disagree with the copy drain plan). resident is a power of two 

542 # >= coreNum, so the [xblock, resident] tile always tiles. 

543 grid = (-(-m_grp // xblock),) 

544 

545 # Row-block pipelining: halve xblock and double the blocks per program, which 

546 # leaves the PROGRAM COUNT (and with it the wave count on 8 clusters) 

547 # untouched while cutting the per-core resident footprint in half and putting 

548 # block i+1's GM read in flight behind block i's compute. Two hard gates: 

549 # divisibility (the pipelined loop has no tail-block protection), and a 

550 # xblock floor of 2 -- xblock == 1 makes the [1, WT] tile LargeN, whose row 

551 # reduce goes cross-core through smem plus a cluster barrier, and paying that 

552 # barrier RITER times per program is exactly the trade this is trying to 

553 # avoid. Only the hold-the-row leg pipelines: the WIDE leg's residency is 

554 # already the segment, not the row. 

555 riter = 1 

556 if not wide: 

557 while ( 

558 xblock > 2 

559 and riter * 2 <= _TLE_FUSE_RITER_MAX 

560 and (xblock // 2) * resident // _TLE_CORE_NUM >= _TLE_FUSE_EPC_PIPE 

561 and m_grp % ((xblock // 2) * (riter * 2)) == 0 

562 ): 

563 xblock //= 2 

564 riter *= 2 

565 grid = (m_grp // (xblock * riter),) if riter > 1 else grid 

566 

567 has_w = weight is not None 

568 has_b = bias is not None 

569 dummy = ( 

570 None 

571 if has_w and has_b 

572 else torch.empty(C, dtype=input.dtype, device=input.device) 

573 ) 

574 w_t = weight if has_w else dummy 

575 b_t = bias if has_b else dummy 

576 # Affine compute dtype: the native input dtype for ALL of fp16/fp32/bf16. 

577 # bf16 needs no explicit f32 detour -- triton/tle-dtype-convert inserts the 

578 # bf16<->f32 conversion implicitly (XPU3 has no bf16 vector op). Only the 

579 # reduce is pinned to f32 for accumulation precision. 

580 cdt = tl_dtype 

581 

582 _tle_group_norm_fused_kernel[grid]( 

583 TensorDescriptor.from_tensor(input.view(m_grp, L), [xblock, WT]), 

584 TensorDescriptor.from_tensor(y.view(m_grp, L), [xblock, WT]), 

585 TensorDescriptor.from_tensor(w_t, [C]), 

586 TensorDescriptor.from_tensor(b_t, [C]), 

587 TensorDescriptor.from_tensor(mean.view(m_grp), [xblock]), 

588 TensorDescriptor.from_tensor(rstd.view(m_grp), [xblock]), 

589 L, 

590 HxW, 

591 eps, 

592 C, 

593 group_size, 

594 group, 

595 xblock, 

596 WT, 

597 _npo2(C), 

598 rb, 

599 wide, 

600 riter, 

601 tl_dtype, 

602 tl_dtype, 

603 cdt, 

604 WT != L, 

605 has_w, 

606 has_b, 

607 isCloseCoreTiling=False, 

608 ) 

609 logger.debug( 

610 "GEMS_KUNLUNXIN NATIVE_GROUP_NORM tle FUSED m_grp=%d L=%d tile=%dx%d " 

611 "wide=%d riter=%d grid=%d", 

612 m_grp, 

613 L, 

614 xblock, 

615 WT, 

616 wide, 

617 riter, 

618 grid[0], 

619 ) 

620 return True 

621 

622 

623def _tle_native_group_norm( 

624 input, y, weight, bias, mean, rstd, N, C, HxW, group, group_size, eps 

625): 

626 """Run group norm as ONE tle kernel; False (untouched) when tle cannot. 

627 

628 On KL3 the fused kernel is the operator: one launch, one kernel, every 

629 shape the aten semantics can produce. group * group_size == C is an aten 

630 invariant (PyTorch's group_norm rejects C % group != 0 at the ATen layer), 

631 so no ragged-group gate is needed here. 

632 """ 

633 if not _TLE_AVAILABLE: 

634 # sum.py declines into its GM-pointer path here; this op has no fallback 

635 # by design, so the same condition has to be a hard error. Failing now 

636 # beats dying inside the tle compile with a much less obvious message. 

637 raise RuntimeError( 

638 "kunlunxin native_group_norm requires the KL3 TLE " 

639 "(TRITON_XPU_ARCH=3 and TRITON_ENABLE_XCN_BACKEND unset)" 

640 ) 

641 if input.dtype not in _TLE_TL_DTYPE: 

642 return False 

643 tl_dtype = _TLE_TL_DTYPE[input.dtype] 

644 m_stat = N * group 

645 lrow = group_size * HxW 

646 

647 with torch_device_fn.device(input.device): 

648 if _tle_group_norm_fused( 

649 input, 

650 y, 

651 weight, 

652 bias, 

653 mean, 

654 rstd, 

655 m_stat, 

656 lrow, 

657 HxW, 

658 C, 

659 group_size, 

660 group, 

661 eps, 

662 tl_dtype, 

663 ): 

664 return True 

665 

666 # The fused kernel covers every shape the aten semantics can produce: wide 

667 # rows go through the in-kernel two-pass segment loop, single rows through 

668 # the m == 1 LargeN tiling. A decline here would mean an unsupported dtype 

669 # or an absurd row width -- both are hard errors worth surfacing rather 

670 # than silently falling back to a kernel that does the same math slower. 

671 raise RuntimeError( 

672 "kunlunxin native_group_norm: tle kernel declined " 

673 f"(N={N} C={C} HxW={HxW} group={group} dtype={input.dtype} " 

674 f"L={group_size * HxW})" 

675 ) 

676 

677 

678def native_group_norm(input, weight, bias, N, C, HxW, group, eps=1e-05): 

679 """aten::native_group_norm on Kunlunxin -- ONE tle.gpu kernel. 

680 

681 The generic flag_gems.ops.native_group_norm binds 

682 flag_gems.ops.groupnorm.group_norm at import time, so SpecOpRegistrar 

683 swapping flag_gems.group_norm never reached it and native_group_norm kept 

684 running the generic single-kernel giant-2D-tile implementation on XPU. 

685 That path miscompiles on the small tiles used by the accuracy matrix and 

686 hard-fails with `out of resource: uni_sram` for HxW >= 4096, so bind a 

687 vendor kernel here explicitly. 

688 

689 There is deliberately no GM-pointer fallback: like sum.py, this vendor 

690 operator is written for the KL3 tle pipeline and only exists there. A second 

691 GM implementation would be a slower duplicate of the same math with none of 

692 the DMA -- it previously existed only to serve shapes the tle kernel could 

693 not tile, and with the m == 1 LargeN tiling and the in-kernel wide-row 

694 segment loop there are no such shapes left. 

695 """ 

696 # The test asserts on the GENERIC spelling ("GEMS NATIVE_GROUP_NORM"), which 

697 # "GEMS_KUNLUNXIN NATIVE_GROUP_NORM" does not contain -- that mismatch alone 

698 # failed all 18 accuracy cases at tests/test_group_norm.py:76, before any 

699 # number was compared. linalg_svd.py carries the vendor tag this way. 

700 logger.debug("GEMS NATIVE_GROUP_NORM (kunlunxin)") 

701 

702 group_size = triton.cdiv(C, group) 

703 input = input.contiguous() 

704 weight = None if weight is None else weight.contiguous() 

705 bias = None if bias is None else bias.contiguous() 

706 

707 y = torch.empty_like(input) 

708 # Returned in the INPUT dtype, like the generic op and groupnorm.py, because 

709 # tests/test_group_norm.py asserts the container dtype through 

710 # gems_assert_close. That used to cost ~20us of a 30us fp16/bf16 kernel (the 

711 # narrow writeback scaled with the ELEMENT size, so 2-byte stats were twice 

712 # as expensive as 4-byte ones); the SM writeback below removes the whole 

713 # penalty for every dtype now that the XPU LLVM backend selects the bf16 SM 

714 # store too. 

715 mean = torch.empty((N, group), dtype=input.dtype, device=input.device) 

716 rstd = torch.empty((N, group), dtype=input.dtype, device=input.device) 

717 

718 _tle_native_group_norm( 

719 input, y, weight, bias, mean, rstd, N, C, HxW, group, group_size, eps 

720 ) 

721 return y, mean, rstd
